# Folio starter books

The book and translation texts are not licensed under the application’s MIT license. Folio includes original literary text, not modern translations, cover art, page scans, publisher logos, ebooks in facsimile, or audiobooks. Each selected text is in the public domain in the United States according to its publisher. This collection also screens the ordinary Kazakhstan and UK terms for the named historical authors and translators. Copyright is territorial. Check local law if distributing elsewhere, and retain authorship and attribution. This is not a worldwide clearance.

Standard Ebooks dedicates its own editorial work under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), not the rights of unrelated authors. Each edition links its publisher page, pinned copyright notice, colophon, source archive, transcription and scan references, individual Unicode source document hashes, and the packaged bytes in [the edition ledger](edition-provenance.json). Only narrative text and specified literary front/back matter are redistributed. Chapter counts may include an epigraph, preface, notes or other reading sections. The three Potter tales are complete, originally separately issued stories. Levels are editorial estimates, not official CEFR levels or adapted graded readers. Historical language and depictions are retained.

Sources and scope: [Standard Ebooks collections policy](https://standardebooks.org/contribute/collections-policy), [U.S. Copyright Office](https://www.copyright.gov/what-is-copyright/), [Kazakhstan Copyright Law, Articles 28–29](https://adilet.zan.kz/eng/docs/Z960000006_), [UK Intellectual Property Office](https://www.gov.uk/copyright/how-long-copyright-lasts). Kazakhstan and UK ordinary terms for identified literary authors run to 70 years after death; in this set even the latest author death is 1947. Kazakhstan protects certain personal non-property rights independently. The 1914 English translation of *Crime and Punishment* is by Constance Garnett (1861–1946); its 1866 original is by Fyodor Dostoevsky (1821–1881). *Frankenstein* includes Mary Shelley's revised 1831 text and the historical preface by Percy Bysshe Shelley (1792–1822). Dates of book publication may differ from earlier magazine serials.
